summary: Demo walkthrough of Redwood Hosted API embeddings and rerank endpoints for Brightnote search relevance use case. Covered high-level flow (embed -> vector DB -> rerank), model choices, latency/cost tradeoffs, Redwood Console observability, and Optimize suggestions. Agreed to run a short benchmark on customer data and share pricing/security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we got Evan our SE and Lina from product. quick roll call?
[00:06] Alex Rivera: Alex here - Head of Search at Brightnote.
[00:08] Priya Shah: Priya here, ML Eng.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan, PM.
[00:12] Evan Park: Evan here. cool to meet you all.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Cool, objective today is a quick walkthrough of Hosted API for embeddings and the rerank endpoint, show how you'd wire it into Brightnote search to improve relevance, and then agree next steps for a short PoC/benchmark. sound good?
[00:28] Alex Rivera: Yep, that's perfect. our main pain is that the vector search returns a lot of false positives; we need reranking with context to bump the right answers.
[00:38] Priya Shah: Also latency sensitive for our web UX — target p95 under 300ms if possible. cost is a big factor too, we run large query volumes.
[00:48] Maya Chen: Got it. Evan — can you show the flow and the endpoints?
[00:52] Evan Park: Sure. I'll share the screen. high level: step one, call the embeddings endpoint to turn your docs into vectors. store those in your vector DB (many customers use Pinecone/Weaviate/Redis). Step two, at query time you do a k-NN nearest neighbor search using your vector store. Step three — here's the key — you call Redwood's rerank endpoint which takes the top N candidates plus the original query and returns a reordered list with relevance scores. that avoids extra round trips to LLMs and is optimized for latency.
[01:20] Jordan Lee: Wait is the rerank done in a separate model or is it scoring using embeddings similarity?
[01:24] Evan Park: Good question. the rerank endpoint uses a lightweight cross-encoder style model (we host variants) that looks at the full query+candidate text pair to produce a relevance score, so it captures signals embeddings similarity may miss. it's more accurate but a bit heavier than vector similarity. we provide tuned variants for latency vs accuracy.
[01:44] Priya Shah: Can you quantify "a bit heavier"? like how much latency delta?
[01:48] Evan Park: on our hosted profiles, typical single-candidate rerank latency at p50 is ~20-40ms on the small/medium rerank models; for batching N=10 candidates you might see p50 around 60-120ms depending on model. so total query flow (knn + rerank) often stays under your 300ms p95 target with the right config. but depends on sequence length.
[02:10] Alex Rivera: And cost — is rerank charged per candidate?
[02:13] Evan Park: Yes it's per-call and per-token where applicable; our pricing model for Hosted API includes per-embedding unit and a per-rerank unit (per candidate scored). We can share SKU details. there are also optimizations: we recommend filtering by metadata first to reduce candidate count, and using Redwood Optimize which will suggest batching/caching and model variants to lower unit costs.
[02:34] Maya Chen: I'll add that our Console shows a per-route cost breakdown so you can see exactly how rerank contributes to spend.
[02:41] Jordan Lee: You mentioned caching — we have a lot of repeated queries. how would caching work with rerank?
[02:46] Evan Park: Two places for caching: prefix / KV caching for generation flows and result caching at the application level for queries with high repeat rate. for rerank specifically, if your query and candidate set is identical, you'll get a cache hit. Optimize will even surface which queries are high-frequency candidates for caching.
[03:05] Priya Shah: Architecturally, we'd like Redwood to be able to run in our VPC later; for now hosted is fine, but security questions: SOC 2, encryption at rest, KMS options?
[03:15] Lina Ortiz: we are SOC 2 Type II, we support TLS in transit and encryption at rest, and for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. hosted customers can also request dedicated tenancy options. we have an audit log stream available to send to your SIEM.
[03:31] Alex Rivera: Great. any limitations for PII redaction or data retention?
[03:35] Lina Ortiz: retention policies are configurable — hosted default retention is 30 days for logs, and we have controls for disabling logging of full content. for regulated customers we typically recommend our Private option or Dedicated with explicit retention SLAs.
[03:47] Jordan Lee: can you run a quick demo of the API call pattern?
[03:50] Evan Park: Yep. I'll paste a condensed flow. first, embeddings call: POST /v1/embeddings with model param like "redwood-embed-v1" and the doc text — returns vectors. store those. at query time: vector db returns top 10 ids; call POST /v1/rerank with payload {query, candidates: [text1...text10], top_k: 5}. the endpoint returns scores and ranked ids. we also support passing metadata blobs so the reranker can use signals like recency or doc type.
[04:22] Alex Rivera: How do you handle long documents? we have long notes and transcripts.
[04:26] Evan Park: we recommend chunking at ingestion (we have libraries and example notebooks). chunk size depends on semantic boundaries and model context window. the reranker works on candidate chunks; you can run a follow-up consolidation pass to merge chunk-level scores into doc-level scores. we showed a notebook with heuristics.
[04:43] Priya Shah: do you provide client libs for batching embeddings? we're currently using a homegrown async approach.
[04:48] Evan Park: yes, SDKs in Python/JS with built-in batching, retry logic, and concurrency tuning. Redwood Optimize can suggest batch sizes for your traffic to hit GPU throughput sweet spots.
[05:00] Jordan Lee: curious about evaluation — how do we know rerank improves our metrics?
[05:04] Evan Park: typical workflow: run an offline eval using a holdout set (we can help scaffold this). you measure nDCG, MRR before and after rerank. we also have A/B rollout hooks in the Console so you can incrementally enable rerank and monitor click-through and latency metrics.
[05:21] Alex Rivera: Mentioned earlier you integrate with vector DBs — would you recommend using your own storage?
[05:26] Evan Park: We don't force a vector store — most customers use a managed vector DB for nearest neighbor. Redwood also offers an optional minimal store for small PoCs, but for production scale we recommend a dedicated vector DB like Pinecone or Redis Vector, and then do rerank in Redwood.
[05:40] Priya Shah: Any demo of tradeoff: accuracy vs cost? like show two rerank model variants?
[05:44] Evan Park: Sure — switching to a trimmed rerank model (redwood-rerank-small) reduces per-candidate latency and cost by ~40% with a small drop in nDCG on internal benchmarks. larger cross-encoder models improve nDCG but cost more. Optimize will recommend the right variant based on your query distribution.
[06:02] Maya Chen: I'll show a quick Console screenshot — apologies for the static share — here you can see per-route latency, cost, token breakdown, and a rerollout control to do canary with automatic rollback on errors.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: that's useful, especially the per-route cost.
[06:21] Alex Rivera: about SLAs — if we go to Dedicated is there an SLA for p95 latency?
[06:26] Lina Ortiz: yes, Dedicated includes capacity guarantees and SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; exact numbers depend on contract. for Hosted we publish performance profiles per model and region.
[06:37] Priya Shah: ok next steps? we'd like a short benchmark: we'll send sample dataset (~5k docs), you provision trial keys, and you run a rerank vs baseline evaluation.
[06:46] Maya Chen: sounds great — we'll do that. Evan you'll own the notebook and run?
[06:49] Evan Park: yep, Evan will share the rerank notebook and run the benchmark with their data if they send it.
[06:55] Alex Rivera: timeline? we want results in two weeks if possible.
[06:58] Maya Chen: we'll aim for two weeks. I'll send pricing and SOC2 pack today. Evan will share code by Tue.
[07:06] Jordan Lee: ok thanks, this was helpful.
[07:08] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items we just discussed.
[07:12] (call ends)
